_comment: Worked example of a mode_hooks declaration. Not loaded: the compiler looks
for <mode_name>.json / .yml, and this file is named EXAMPLE so it never
matches a mode. Copy it, rename it to your mode, and replace the numbers.
The core ships the gate implementation and supplies no thresholds of its
own. Every number, pattern, and message below belongs to the mode. That is
the whole split: the core guarantees a declared norm is checkable, never

binding._comment: Pins this declaration to a revision of the mode body. When the body moves on, mode_hooks_validate reports DRIFT instead of silently enforcing yesterday's numbers. Omit the whole object to opt out of drift detection.

Stop._blocking_note: false on purpose in the example. The vocabulary rule below is the one thing here that cannot be got right by reading: whether a shape is coined shorthand or an ordinary technical word depends on what you write about. Start in report-only mode, read your log for a week, then set this to true. Shipping the example with true meant a consumer who copied it as instructed was blocked on the first message mentioning a character encoding.

params._diagram_note: A floor rather than a cap: over this many lines of prose, a message carrying no fenced block is reported. Omit the key to leave the floor off. Announcing the length does not clear it — an announcement says the message is long, not that prose was the right carrier.
params._shorthand_note: Two rules this example exists to carry. Bound the digit count on any lowercase branch: coined shorthand is short (t0, a9), while a git commit id or a content hash is long, and an unbounded quantifier reports those as undefined vocabulary on every message that cites one. And write character classes in POSIX form, never as the ASCII-only shorthand: the ASCII form does not match full-width digits, so a mode enforcing this rule on Japanese text silently passed every token written with them.
params._uppercase_branch_note: Deliberately absent. A branch matching uppercase letters welded to digits catches coined labels, and it also catches UTF-8, SHA-256, MD5, S3, EC2 and TLS1 — 12 of 17 ordinary technical words in one measurement. There is no shape that separates the two, so this example ships without the branch rather than shipping a trap. Add it only after measuring against your own writing. The lowercase branch below has the same problem in miniature and is kept anyway: it matches a9 and t0, and it also matches x86. That residual is the reason blocking is false above.
params.rewrite_instruction: Rewrite it. Cut preamble and restatement; never cut facts, numbers with their denominator, uncertainty, or worked examples.

not_gated.reason: states an orientation, not a limit. Violating it leaves no trace in any artifact, so there is nothing a gate could measure.
